Embassy of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in Ankara Kuzey Kıbrıs Türk Cumhuriyeti'nin Ankara Büyükelçiliği
The Embassy of Northern Cyprus in Ankara is the diplomatic mission of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus to the Republic of Turkey. It is located in the Gaziosmanpaşa district of Ankara.

The incumbent ambassador is İsmet Korukoğlu since 14 September 2022.

The existence of an embassy is controversial as the Republic of Cyprus and the international community see Northern Cyprus as occupied territory. However, Turkey recognizes it as an independent state and maintains diplomatic relations. Northern Cyprus is recognized by the international community as a de facto state.

History
The Embassy of Northern Cyprus in Ankara was established in 17 April 1984, shortly after the declaration of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Prior to 1984, the institution existed in various names. In 1966, the Turkish Cypriot Community in Cyprus established an Ankara Office, which became the Representation of the Autonomous Turkish Cypriot Administration in Ankara in 1974. In 1975, it was renamed as the Representation of the Head of the Turkish Cypriot Federated State, and in 1983, it began to serve as an Embassy. Since then, the embassy has played an important role in maintaining diplomatic relations between Northern Cyprus and Turkey.

Services
The Embassy of Northern Cyprus in Ankara provides a range of services to Turkish Cypriot citizens living in Turkey and Turkish citizens who wish to visit or travel to Northern Cyprus. These services include consular services, such as passport and identity document issuance, and assistance with legal and financial issues.

List of representatives
The ambassador is the chief diplomat of Northern Cyprus in Turkey and is responsible for overseeing the embassy's activities and representing Northern Cyprus' interests in Turkey. As of 2023, the Ambassador of Northern Cyprus to Turkey is İsmet Korukoğlu.

Consulates and Embassies in Northern Cyprus operate under a unique diplomatic framework due to the region’s special political status. Officially known as the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), this region is recognized only by Turkey, which means it does not host the same number of embassies and consulates found in most internationally recognized countries.
However, several nations maintain representative offices, visa branches, or information desks — often referred to as informal embassies — mainly located in Lefkoşa (the capital of Northern Cyprus).
This article reviews the legal and practical status of Embassies and Consulates in Northern Cyprus, provides a complete list of active offices with their contact details, and explains the types of services they offer. Legal and Diplomatic Status of Embassies in Northern Cyprus

From a legal perspective, the diplomatic status of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) is both unique and complex. At present, Turkey is the only country that officially recognizes the TRNC as an independent state. As a result, most foreign missions operating in the northern part of the island are not regarded as official embassies, but instead as representative offices, visa service branches, or information desks.
According to the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the TRNC, only the Embassy of Turkey in Lefkoşa holds full diplomatic accreditation. Other countries — such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Australia, and France — maintain smaller offices that provide limited consular and informational services within Northern Cyprus.

The **Embassy of Turkey** in North Nicosia is the sole embassy in Northern Cyprus as the rest of the international community locate their embassies to the Cyprus island in the Republic of Cyprus. The island is divided between four sides; the unrecognised Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus to the north, the internationally recognised Republic of Cyprus to the south, the United Nations buffer zone separating the two, and the British overseas territories of Akrotiri and Dhekelia. The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus is only recognised by Turkey, therefore its embassy is in the capital North Nicosia. Turkey does not recognise the Republic of Cyprus. The incumbent ambassador is Metin Feyzioğlu since 28 November 2022.

## History

In June 1925, Consulate of Turkey to Cyprus (Turkish: *Türkiye Şehbenderliği*) opened in Larnaca. It was connected to Turkish Embassy in London. The consulate then moved to Nicosia in 1939. The new building was reflecting the traditional Turkish Cypriot architecture. After signing of the Zurich and London Treaties, the consulate in Nicosia became an embassy in 1960. Following the Turkish invasion of Cyprus, the embassy became very close to the UN Buffer Zone. It moved to across the Turkish Northern Cyprus Parliament Building in 1978. The chancery and the residence is still located in the same place.

## Sub-divisions

Northern Cyprus is recognized by the international community as a de facto state. The Embassy of Northern Cyprus in Ankara was established in 17 April 1984, shortly after the declaration of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Prior to 1984, the institution existed in various names.

Since then, the embassy has played an important role in maintaining diplomatic relations between Northern Cyprus and Turkey.
The Embassy of Northern Cyprus in Ankara is the diplomatic mission of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus to the Republic of Turkey. It is located in the Gaziosmanpaşa district of Ankara. The incumbent ambassador is İsmet Korukoğlu since 14 September 2022.
